## THE FAILURE THIS TIMER EXISTS TO PREVENT

Tyler, after catching it happen:

> "the whole point of the 20 minute tmer is to make sure you never ever stop
> like you just did. fix that"

**Writing prose to the user is stopping.** A status summary is stopping. A
bulleted recap of what landed is stopping. Ending a turn because a milestone
felt tidy is stopping. None of those are reports — they are the thing the
standing rule forbids.

What triggered it: three commits landed, the territory overlay was left
visibly rendering as stripes instead of a body, and instead of fixing it the
session wrote "Where things stand" and handed control back. Leaving something
broken on the demo screen to write a summary is the worst available trade.

**The only acceptable end to a turn is running out of context, or Tyler
interrupting.** Not a milestone. There is always a next task.

The timer now fires every 8 minutes rather than 20, because 20 was long enough
to drift into a report.

## What this prompt requires, as a checklist

Every 20 minutes, confirm each of these is still true:

1. **The two brainstorm files are being used.** `docs/sources/BRAINSTORM-1-hardware-list.md`
   and `docs/sources/BRAINSTORM-2-vision.md`. Re-explain them to yourself each
   cycle. The vision is an **AI wheelchair with 4 arms** doing shower, eating
   and pill feeding, vitals, and voice control. Not just a scrubbing demo.
2. **ECC is being used to its full potential.** `/tmp/ECC`, 292 skills, agents,
   commands, rules. Installed at `.claude/`. No excuse for not using it.
3. **No stalling.** Is the current task the highest-ROI thing available? If a
   blocker appeared, that is not a stop condition — there is always something
   high-ROI. Switch to it.
4. **The merge is happening.** `scrub3d` (backend: body scan, 4-arm partition,
   tracking, safety) plus `main` (frontend: cartoon, HUD, juice) into one
   application. This is co-equal with fleshing out the vision.
5. **Nothing is being hand-built that could be taken.** Search GitHub, npm,
   asset libraries, Claude Code skills FIRST, every time. Write down what was
   searched.
6. **Commits are frequent.** Each landing committed and pushed.
7. **Progress is documented.** `docs/PROGRESS.md` updated as work lands, so
   time is not lost re-deriving state.
8. **Priority order is right.** Technically and visually impressive for a
   **demonstration** outranks everything. Bugs are the lowest priority. If it
   works in a presentation, that is good enough.
